$comment: Template for a registry that includes PAID models.
Every non-zero price must carry `priceVerifiedAt` (YYYY-MM-DD) or the file is
rejected at load time. This is enforced, not advisory: a stale price does not
fail loudly, it silently reorders the `cheap` profile, and you find out from
the invoice. Open the provider's pricing page, copy the numbers, stamp the date.
The prices below are ZEROED ON PURPOSE so this file cannot be used as-is and
cannot pretend to be a price list. Fill them in yourself.
Privacy tiers are yours to assign and are the one filter routing will never
override. Give a provider `internal` unless you have actually read its data
retention terms; give it `confidential` only if you have a DPA saying so.

providers.$comment2: maxConcurrent counts the requests in flight right now; quota counts them over a window. A fan-out hits maxConcurrent first, with the per-minute budget barely touched. Omit it for unlimited; do not guess a number.
providers.$comment3: Scope matters more than the figure. A limit published for the API key belongs here, on the provider, and every model behind that key shares it — write it on each model instead and three models admit three times the account's budget, while the 429 that follows looks like any other failure. Both numbers here are placeholders: replace them with limits you have read in the provider's own documentation.

models.$comment: A quota here is this model's alone, and sits inside the account's: it is the shape for a preview or a promotional model that is capped more tightly than the key that reaches it. Placeholder, like the rest.

providers.$comment: vLLM / llama.cpp / Ollama. The only tier that can honestly be 'highly_confidential', because the bytes never leave the box.
providers.$comment2: A local server has one GPU and a real queue depth, so this is the case where the number is knowable: set it to what your server actually runs in parallel.
